the spatial patterns of AFSC in central Sumatra and the future changes under three forest policy scenarios.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AFCS maps and scenarios presented here are useful in the planning of REDD + projects in the study region and in other regions of tropical Asia.
the time-series maps of AFCS in the forests of Sumatra can be used for the planning of REDD+ projects in the study region.

the time-series AFCS map provides spatially and temporally explicit scenarios of AFCS change, which may aid planning REDD+ in the study area and stimulate the development and implementation of similar AFCS maps in other tropical Asian regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for estimating the AFCS and their changes in tropical Asia, and applied it to a large area in Riau province.
the time-series AFCS map is a powerful tool to assess the carbon emission risk and to design REDD+ projects in the Riau Province of Sumatra.
the spatial patterns of AFSC and their trends under three scenarios vary on a large scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatially explicit modeling of AFCS is a useful approach to assess the potential impact of forest management and policy scenarios in tropical Asia.
, although the AFCS maps are spatially explicit, the trends in AFCS are highly uncertain and vary on a local-scale.

, in the context of REDD+, it is important to take into account local differences in the spatial pattern of AFCS and to recognize that different forest policy scenarios can lead to significantly different AFCS changes.
